expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription with status literals in each

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each interface extends SubscriptionBase then adds only its own fields—trialEndsAt, renewsAt, retryCount+gracePeriodEndsAt, or cancellation respectively

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never) {...} with default: return assertNever(sub) in nextBillingEvent switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type SubscriptionId = string & { readonly __brand: 'SubscriptionId' }; type CustomerId = ...; type PlanId = ...

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'Illegal transitions (canceled → trialing) aren't expressed here — that's a separate transition(sub, event) function' but does not provide it

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: **What this makes impossible** section explicitly lists: 'Fields from the wrong state', 'Missing required fields', 'Swapping customerId and planId', 'A cancellation that says voluntary but gives involuntary reason', 'Forgetting a status in a switch'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Opens: 'a flat {status, trialEndsAt?, retryCount?, ...} claims 2⁵ = 32 field combinations are legal when only 4 are' then recommends union
